content:
- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history; model reacts too aggressively, peaking too soon.
- Underestimates downward trends or mean-reverting periods; fails to recognize price pullback after peaks.
- Late forecast days (last 5–10) often show underestimation, possibly due to lag or insufficient recent data weighting.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent high prices.
- When history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., after 75+), model fails to adjust downward quickly enough.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows tendency to smooth out volatility; misses short-term reversals or sudden drops.
- Model often ignores recent low prices in history, leading to underestimation when true outcome dips.
